independence.post_lock_policy: Do not change this rubric after inspecting Reviewer A or B. If a material defect is discovered, preserve this file and create a new version before restarting adjudication.

scope.adjudication_scope: Symbolic ontology and governance contract only

source_artifacts.role: Machine-readable v1 questions, approved invariants, required changes, blockers, and expert recommendations
Review summary, structural findings, remaining blockers, and execution boundary
Human-readable rendering of the v1 ledger
External design rationale for P0 corrections and family-specific changes

observed_baseline.original_pasted_review_limit: The source states that it was a static review and did not re-run the repository test suite.

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Exact current v2 machine-readable fields, invariants, family graphs, formula entries, registries, and content hashes
evidence_hierarchy.rule: Use the current v2 artifact as the proposition actually being adjudicated.

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Repository validator and targeted CPU-only test behavior for mechanically enforceable claims
evidence_hierarchy.rule: A machine-enforceable claim is not considered fully closed when it exists only as prose or an unenforced flag.

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: V1 ledger questions, approved invariants, required changes, blocking items, and unresolved references
evidence_hierarchy.rule: Use these to define what each inherited assumption must discharge; do not inherit the old disposition automatically.

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: V2 review and v1-to-v2 diff documents
evidence_hierarchy.rule: Use as traceability and rationale; resolve any conflict against the exact current machine-readable artifact and observed validator behavior.
Use as unsigned design input, not as approval, runtime proof, identity proof, or freeze proof.
Use to enforce scope, sequencing, and the separate human-freeze gate.

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Reviewer A and Reviewer B outputs after rubric lock
evidence_hierarchy.rule: Treat as advisory analyses that must cite higher-ranked evidence; agreement is not proof and disagreement is not resolved by voting.

core_invariants: Online ontology state and evidence are prefix-only and causally timestamped.
Future-visible completion and outcome data remain in separate namespaces and are not runtime inputs.
Ontology structure does not encode trading actions, profit claims, or future-effect certainty.
Morphology, structural orientation, semantic role, and future outcome are distinct concepts.
Terminal objects are immutable; later formations require new object identity.
Cross-family and cross-scale relations do not destructively merge object identity.
Committed anchors use closed bars and append-only revision lineage.
Price geometry is normalized or dimensionless; absolute-price detector thresholds are forbidden in the ontology core.
Train-selected policy is fit on the training partition only and cannot be selected from validation or test outcomes.
Unknown and inapplicable inputs remain explicitly masked.
Ambiguity and insufficient evidence are permitted and block gold eligibility.
No AI output is independent human gold truth or human freeze approval.

ACCEPT.definition: The exact technical proposition is complete, coherent, causal, and unambiguously represented by the current v2 symbolic contract.
required_conditions: Every essential component of the question has concrete v2 evidence paths.
Every relevant v1 required change and blocking item is RESOLVED or demonstrably NOT_APPLICABLE.
Mechanically enforceable constraints have validator or targeted test evidence, when such enforcement is part of the contract.
No essential empirical, train-fitted, registry, annotation, or identity evidence is missing.
No contradiction with the core invariants remains.
ACCEPT.human_freeze_effect: NONE; simulated ACCEPT is non-binding and cannot satisfy the human-freeze gate.

REVISE.definition: The design direction is supportable, but the current proposition is incomplete, ambiguous, internally inconsistent, too broad, too narrow, or missing an exact contract or enforcement binding.
required_output: Name the exact incomplete or conflicting component.
Cite the current evidence path and the unsatisfied v1 blocker or invariant.
Specify the smallest concrete contract, validator, or wording change needed.
Do not invent a numeric threshold or train-fitted value.

DEFER.definition: The proposition cannot be decided now because an essential fact intentionally lies outside the available symbolic evidence.
valid_triggers: An authoritative calendar, instrument, or external registry is required but unavailable.
A numeric value, clipping bound, normalizer artifact, threshold, or policy must be selected from train-partition evidence.
Real-data examples, human annotation evidence, reviewer agreement, calibration, or empirical performance are essential to the proposition.
Verified human appointment, authority, or independence is itself the proposition under review.
invalid_triggers: GPU and training are deferred, when the proposition is purely symbolic.
The v1 ledger used DEFER, when v2 now supplies complete symbolic evidence.
A real human freeze is globally absent, when the per-assumption technical proposition can still be judged.
required_output: Explain why it is essential rather than downstream implementation detail.
State the non-GPU or future empirical event that will make the question decidable.

REJECT.definition: The proposition is fundamentally unsound or directly conflicts with confirmed ontology, causality, identity, normalization, leakage, or governance invariants and cannot be repaired by a narrow revision.
valid_triggers: It uses future-visible or trading semantics as online ontology input.
It treats morphology as guaranteed future effect without causal context.
It permits same-object terminal reset, destructive identity merge, or committed partial-bar history.
It permits absolute-price core thresholds or validation/test-selected policy.
It treats model-assisted or AI agreement as independent human gold truth or freeze approval.
Its object, phase, anchor, relation, or formula semantics are irreconcilable with the confirmed core invariants.
required_output: Explain why a narrow revision is insufficient.
Specify removal or a replacement proposition.

decision_algorithm: Verify the assumption ID and exact question against the 61-ID inherited registry or 9-ID new-v2 registry.
Decompose the question into essential components without changing its scope.
For inherited assumptions, enumerate every v1 approved invariant, required change, blocking item, and unresolved parameter reference.
Map each component and v1 item to exact v2 contract paths and, where mechanically enforceable, validator or targeted test evidence.
Check for a direct contradiction with core invariants. A confirmed fundamental contradiction yields REJECT.
Check whether an essential component requires unavailable external, empirical, train-fitted, annotation, or identity evidence. If yes and no known contradiction already controls, yield DEFER.
Check whether all components are conceptually supportable but any current contract detail or enforcement is incomplete. If yes, yield REVISE.
Yield ACCEPT only when all essential components pass and no relevant blocker or dependency remains.
For a conjunctive assumption with mixed component outcomes, record component findings and use the most restrictive essential-component outcome in this order: REJECT, DEFER, REVISE, ACCEPT.
Record evidence, uncertainty, required follow-up, and the separate non-binding human-freeze status.

principles: The v1 disposition is historical evidence, not the v2 adjudication result.
A v1 DEFER may become ACCEPT or REVISE when v2 supplies the missing symbolic object, phase, anchor, relation, or formula contract.
A v1 REVISE may become ACCEPT only after every essential required change and blocker is explicitly discharged.
Copying an assumption ID into v2 is lineage only and never resolves a blocker by itself.
A prose claim that a blocker is resolved is insufficient when the corresponding exact v2 field or invariant is absent.
A policy flag alone is insufficient when the promised machine-enforceable behavior is not validated.

No numeric detector threshold is required for accepting a symbolic contract that intentionally forbids numeric thresholds; a question that explicitly requires selecting such a value remains DEFER or REVISE according to its wording.

blocker_statuses.RESOLVED: The v2 contract explicitly satisfies the full blocker and supporting enforcement exists where mechanically applicable.
blocker_statuses.PARTIALLY_RESOLVED: V2 addresses the direction but one or more essential fields, states, branches, formulas, registries, or enforcement bindings remain missing.
blocker_statuses.OPEN: No adequate v2 evidence discharges the blocker.
blocker_statuses.NOT_APPLICABLE: V2 deliberately removed or superseded the old premise, with an explicit replacement contract and rationale.

rules: Do not run or request GPU, JAX, training, detector, labeler, real-label, or synthetic-sample work for this adjudication.
Do not penalize a purely symbolic ontology proposition because execution flags are false.
ACCEPT may cover a precise train-only fit boundary, versioning rule, hash requirement, or missingness policy without fitting an artifact.
DEFER any essential numeric value or fitted artifact that cannot exist until the declared train-partition procedure runs.
Do not use downstream predictive or trading performance to validate morphology existence or ontology semantics.

human_identity_and_authority_policy.separation_rule: Per-assumption technical disposition and global human-freeze eligibility are separate outputs.
human_identity_and_authority_policy.personal_data_requirement: No personal data is required; pseudonymous reviewer IDs are compatible with the v2 policy.
minimum_identity_provenance_for_real_hum: A pseudonymous reviewer ID bound outside the public artifact to a real human reviewer
Recorded role and explicit appointment or approval authority
Independence attestation for the two reviewers
Decision timestamps and hash-bound reviewed artifact
current_ai_evidence: The v1 ledger identifies CODEX_DOMAIN_EXPERT_01 as USER_APPOINTED_AI_DOMAIN_EXPERT.
AI_SIMULATED_ADJUDICATOR is not a real human reviewer or approver.
Reviewer A and B outputs, if AI-generated, remain advisory regardless of agreement.
rules: Missing real-human authority does not automatically DEFER every technical assumption.
A technically ACCEPTed assumption still has human_review_required=true and freeze_eligible=false in this simulated adjudication.
Even 70 simulated ACCEPT decisions cannot set human_review.status, frozen, approver, approved_at, frozen_sha256, or reviewer_decisions_recorded.
MG1-B remains BLOCKED until the repository-defined human, hash, provenance, and validation gates are actually satisfied.

ingestion_preconditions: This rubric file exists and its SHA-256 is recorded before either reviewer output is opened.
Each reviewer output declares reviewer identity type, authority, reviewed artifact hash, and whether it is human or AI.
Each output contains exactly the same 70 unique assumption IDs with a valid disposition and cited evidence.
rules: Do not use majority voting or average confidence.
Matching A/B dispositions are re-evaluated against this rubric and do not auto-pass.
Conflicting dispositions are independently resolved using the evidence hierarchy and decision algorithm.
Unsupported ACCEPT claims are downgraded according to the observed gap, not preserved for consensus.
Missing assumptions, silent defaults, vague citations, or rationale that only restates a disposition are insufficient evidence.
Record both reviewer positions faithfully before issuing the adjudicated result.

completion_gate_for_later_70_item_adjudi: Exactly 70 unique assumption IDs are present: 61 inherited and 9 new.
No assumption has a missing or implicit disposition.
Every inherited assumption includes a disposition for each relevant v1 blocker and required change.
Every ACCEPT cites complete current-v2 evidence and has no open essential blocker.
Every REVISE states a minimal exact change.
Every DEFER states the exact evidence and resume condition.
Every REJECT cites a direct contradiction and replacement or removal path.
Disposition counts sum to 70 and are independently recomputed.
The adjudication report states that it is non-binding and cannot freeze v2 or unblock MG1-B.

required_before_real_freeze: Two independent real-human decisions for all 70 assumptions
Adjudication of every disagreement and ambiguity
No remaining REVISE, DEFER, or REJECT disposition in the artifact proposed for freeze
Final file hashes, resolved-contract hash, and review-record hash
Reviewer and adjudication provenance bound to the reviewed hashes
Structural validation of the final reviewed artifact

prohibited_reasoning: Do not infer acceptance from assumption-ID inheritance.
Do not infer acceptance solely from prose saying a structural issue was resolved.
Do not carry v1 REVISE or DEFER forward without re-evaluating current v2 evidence.
Do not use deferred GPU or training as a reason to reject a symbolic contract.
Do not invent thresholds, fitted artifacts, registry contents, human identities, or approval records.
Do not equate AI agreement with two independent real-human decisions.
Do not use future outcomes or trading returns to define online morphology.
Do not treat missing personal data as missing reviewer identity when valid pseudonymous provenance exists.
Do not resolve A/B disagreement by majority, confidence averaging, or deference to the more permissive reviewer.
Do not present a hypothesis as a confirmed conclusion without exact evidence.
